text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London ended higher by the close on industry and trade price fixing, helped by soaring New York values, traders said. Roasters and traders were reported to have jumped in to fix prices of their earlier contracts as the market took an upward path. Many also rolled forward their May positions ahead of the contract's first notice day. Benchmark May rebounded from a low of $1,550 a tonne to end the day $15 higher at $1,585 a tonne. The May/July spread narrowed to level money by the close, against a $6 premium on Tuesday.

Arabica futures in New York finished sharply higher, with the May contract jumping some 6 percent, on chart-driven speculative buying amid a background of continued supply concerns, dealers said. May settled up 10.95 cents/lb at 189.70 cents/lb after trading from 190.00 to 177.10. Second month July settled 8.65 cents/lb higher at 173.15 cents/lb, while the back months closed up 6.00 to down 0.75 cents/lb. Upward momentum accelerated after May rose through the 180.00- cent level, touching off commission house buy-stops around 183.00, then 185.00 cents.

Strength in the nearby May/July switch which widened to 16.55 cents from 14.25 on Tuesday bolstered the market, traders said. Additionally, a lack of selling by origins which were reportedly well sold contributed to the upswing. After Wednesday's close, the CSCE reported certified coffee stocks were off 250 60-kg bags, to 81,578 bags as of April 8. There were no bags pending grading, the exchange added.

BRAZIL - Brazilian coffee exports in March totalled 1.39 million 60-kg bags against 514,606 bags in the same month last year, the Brazilian Coffee Exporters' Association (Abecafe) said. The March total is based on figures from the Industry and Commerce Ministry, Abecafe said in a statement. In the first three months of this year, shipments reached 3.89 million bags, 124 percent up on the 1.74 million bags exported in January to March 1996. Abecafe estimates that shipments in 1997 will reach 16.1 million bags, representing a 24 percent rise on 1996.

GERMANY - Coffee imports in November 1996 amounted to 1.257 million bags, up from 1.148 million bags imported in November 1995. This brought cumulative imports in the first eleven months of 1996 (January/November) up to 12.399 million bags, 5.3 percent up on the tonnage imported in the like period the previous year. Total imports in 1995 reached 12.897 million bags, down from 13.671 million bags imported in 1994.

Major suppliers of green coffee in January/November 1996 were Colombia (2.273 million vs 3.117 million bags), El Salvador (1.131 million vs 1.012 million bags), Indonesia (770,500 vs 354,500 bags) and Brazil (756,900 vs 749,900 bags). Coffee exports in November 1996 amounted to 395,250 bags, up from 267,358 bags in November 1995. This brought cumulative exports in January/November 1996 up to 3.487 million bags, 21.5 percent up on the volume exported in the same year ago period. Total exports in 1995 amounted to 3.238 million bags against 3.514 million bags in 1994.

German coffee exports are mainly in the form of roast and ground with Belgium- Luxembourg (362,900 vs 304,000 bags), the Netherlands (319,200 vs 275,300 bags) and France (116,100 vs 112,500 bags) being the main markets.
